newsitem.title: UK: HORSE RACING-CLASSIC WINNER IN SHERGAR-STYLE SHOW.
newsitem.headline: HORSE RACING-CLASSIC WINNER IN SHERGAR-STYLE SHOW.

text.p: Entrepreneur, showing even more speed than the mighty Shergar, swept to a majestic victory on Saturday in the 2,000 Guineas, the first classic of the British season.
It was a bitter-sweet victory for trainer Michael Stoute as his long-time jockey Walter Swinburn has had to take a break from riding because of weight problems.
Entrepreneur was steered to victory by big race specialist Michael Kinane who said: "I dedicate this one to Walter."

Entrepreneur, who hit the front over three furlongs (600 metres) out had a dream run up the rail. The colt ran out a three quarters of a length winner at odds of 11-2 from the fast finishing 100-30 favourite Revoque, with the 9-1 shot Poteen third one and a half lengths back.

Stoute, who has been conquering tracks all round the world from Japan to Dubai to the U.S. with his stable stars Singspiel and Pilsudski, said that Entrepreneur would now go straight for the Derby and he was confident he could handle the tricky Epsom switchback track.
Bookmakers have installed Entrepreneur as a warm 7-4 favourite.
Stoute, who trained the mighty Shergar to win the Epsom Derby in 1981, said of Entrepreneur: "He has more speed than Shergar. I would be very hopeful that he would get the Derby trip (2.4 km).
"From the moment we started serious work with him as a two-year-old, he has exuded class."
Entrepreneur, a son of top sire Sadler's Wells, was at 600,000 guineas ($1 million) the joint-most expensive horse to be sold at Newmarket's Houghton's yearling sales in 1995.

Stoute, who produced Entrepreneur fighting fit to win his first race of the season for former bookmaker Michael Tabor, said:"He really is a perfectly balanced horse and he has got much more speed than you expect."
It was the third victory in the 2,000 Guineas for Stoute and the second for Kinane, the former Irish champion jockey.

Kinane, who tucked Entrepreneur in about sixth place behind the early leaders Starborough and Shii-Take, said:" I was in the firing line four and a half furlongs out and I had to commit him earlier than I wanted to.
"He travels so easily and took the race by the scruff of the neck. I was always holding John Reid (rider of Revoque)."
Kinane did not forget Swinburn's misfortune afterwards, wishing him a speedy return to the saddle.
"I hope he will get back to where he deserves," he said of Swinburn, who rode two Derby winners for Stoute -- Shergar and Shahrastani.
